question: How do I vote?
answer:
If you haven't already recieved a mail in ballot, you can go in person to a polling center and pick up a ballot, or vote in person on June 30th. If you're not registered yet, you will need your: name, birthday, address, and a Drivers License number, State ID number, or SSN.

question: What is the deadline to register to vote?
answer:
In Colorado, you can register to vote up until and including Election Day, which is November 3rd for the 2026 Midterm General election. Make sure you have your name, birthday, address, and a Drivers License number, State ID number, or SSN ready.

question: Why are there so many confusing ballot items? How can voters be expected to be informed on every item?
answer:
Colorado’s ballot is largely shaped by a combination of dark money political spending and TABOR.

Groups such as [Advance Colorado](http://whoisadvancecolorado.org) (Prop 81, 82, 83, 84, 85, 86, 132, 136) and Protect Kids Colorado (Prop 133, 134, 135) have backed measures in this guide, showing how organized, well-funded interests can use ballot campaigns to advance their priorities. Voters deserve clear information about who is funding these campaigns and whose interests they serve. Better yet, money should not have any influence over our democracy.

While money in politics is a issue across the country, Colorado's very own TABOR also creates a unique set of issues. TABOR limits how much revenue local governments can keep and spend. TABOR can be directly blamed for the frequent "Sophie's Choice" scenarios voters face- having to choose between basic public services (education, healthcare, etc.) and other priorities (climate, infrastructure, etc.). This feels unnatural when we live in one of the wealthiest states in the wealthiest country in the world.

question: What is the Green New Deal?
answer:
The Green New Deal is an ever-updating set of policy goals which would take the steps to address the climate crisis, socioeconomic inequality and injustice, and allow a liveable future for us all.

You can read more [here](https://www.sunrisemovement.org/green-new-deal/).
